Online Master of Science in Sport Management

Prepare for leadership in the sport industry with Texas Tech’s fully online Master of Science in Sport Management. This 30-credit-hour program develops strategic, operational and revenue-focused expertise for careers in collegiate athletics, professional sports and sport-related organizations.

Texas Tech University’s Online Master of Science in Sport Management is a 30-credit-hour graduate program designed to prepare students for leadership and administrative roles across the sport industry. The curriculum combines core management principles with specialized coursework in sport law, marketing, revenue generation, player personnel management and organizational leadership. Delivered fully online in an asynchronous format, the program is structured for working professionals seeking advancement in collegiate athletics, professional sport organizations, community recreation and related industries. Students build analytical, financial and strategic decision-making skills while examining the legal, operational and ethical dimensions of sport enterprises. Emphasis is placed on applied learning and industry relevance, preparing graduates to navigate the competitive and evolving landscape of the global sport industry with confidence and strategic insight.

Bachelor's degree from any accredited institution. No GMAT/GRE is required.

Online Bachelor of Applied Arts & Sciences in Emergency Management

The Bachelor of Applied Arts and Sciences (BAAS) in Emergency Management is a fully online completer program designed for students who have earned an Associate of Applied Science (AAS) in emergency management, fire science or a related field from an accredited community college.

Emergency management is a vital and rapidly evolving profession focused on safeguarding communities against natural, technological and human-made hazards. Texas Tech University has designed this curriculum to provide graduates with the advanced knowledge and skills needed to succeed in this demanding field. This degree builds on foundational knowledge gained in associate programs, combined with professional experience, to deliver a strong upper-level core based on all-hazards principles.

Students study hazard identification and risk assessment, emergency planning and preparedness, incident command, disaster recovery, continuity planning, mitigation strategies, resilience building, leadership, crisis communication, and policy, legal and ethical issues. Courses are delivered entirely online in an asynchronous 8-week format.

The program emphasizes real-world application through case studies, simulations, peer discussions and a capstone project. Students build on their professional experience while strengthening skills in interagency coordination, ethical decision-making and policy development. They also learn from faculty with extensive industry experience and connect with peers to build valuable professional networks.

Online Master of Agribusiness (MAB)

Advance your career in today’s evolving agricultural economy with Texas Tech’s 100% online Master of Agribusiness. This 36-credit-hour graduate program integrates economic analysis, finance, law and emerging technology to prepare professionals for strategic leadership in global agribusiness.

The Online Master of Agribusiness at Texas Tech University prepares professionals to lead in a complex, data-driven agricultural marketplace. This 36-credit-hour graduate program blends analytical rigor from the Department of Agricultural and Applied Economics with business insight from the Rawls College of Business, creating a distinctive combination of economic, financial and management training. Students develop advanced expertise in market analysis, agribusiness management, financial strategy, regulatory frameworks and quantitative modeling. They apply economic theory and financial principles to real-world challenges across agricultural production, commodity markets, agribusiness firms, financial institutions and global food systems. Coursework strengthens the ability to evaluate pricing dynamics, manage risk, interpret policy impacts and make data-informed strategic decisions. A dedicated course in generative artificial intelligence for agribusiness introduces emerging technologies that support forecasting, operational efficiency and innovation. Delivered fully online in an asynchronous format, the program offers flexibility for working professionals while maintaining rigorous graduate-level standards. The program is ranked No. 1 in the nation for Online Master’s Degrees in Agricultural Business by Best College Reviews.

Prepare for Texas school counselor certification with Texas Tech’s online Master of Education in School Counseling. This 48-credit-hour graduate program integrates counseling theory, ethical practice, diversity, assessment and supervised practicum experience in K–12 settings.

Online Advanced School Counseling Certificate

The Advanced School Counseling Certificate is designed for professionals who have already earned a master’s degree in counseling and are seeking to become certified school counselors in Texas. The certificate includes the coursework and supervised practicum required by the Texas Education Agency (TEA) for certification. Candidates complete a 160-hour supervised practicum in an approved Texas K–12 school setting under the supervision of a qualified school counselor and in accordance with Texas Tech University’s Educator Preparation Program (EPP) requirements.

This certificate is intended for individuals who already hold a master’s degree in counseling and wish to expand their professional practice into the K–12 educational setting without completing an additional master’s degree.

Completion of the certificate satisfies the educational and practicum requirements for Texas School Counselor certification through Texas Tech University’s approved Educator Preparation Program. Candidates must also meet all applicable Texas Education Agency certification requirements, including passing the required certification examination and any additional state requirements in effect at the time of application for certification.

The curriculum maps to core content areas tested on the CPA exam — including Financial Accounting and Reporting (FAR), Auditing and Attestation (AUD), Taxation and Regulation (REG) and Information Systems and Controls (ISC) — while developing technical proficiency and professional competencies needed in public accounting, industry and non-profit environments. Students study taxation, auditing, accounting information systems, advanced accounting topics, ethics and business law. Delivered fully online and asynchronously, the program provides flexibility for working professionals and prepares graduates to excel as accounting practitioners, leaders and strategic contributors in a wide range of organizations.

Yes, limits depend on the degree applicability towards a chosen program and residency requirements.

This means you are not viewing the certificate through your Texas Tech’s learning program. chunks.text:
Non-credit

Courses or certificates that do not count for university credit toward a degree.

Peer-reviewed assignment

An assignment graded by other learners in the class; you often must both submit and review a number of peers’ submissions.

Reset deadlines

A Coursera feature that lets learners change suggested completion dates for a course when they miss the original schedule; it extends suggested target dates but does not remove course requirements.

Self-paced / on-demand learning

Course format that lets learners complete material at their own speed rather than following fixed meeting times or deadlines.

How much does the 10-K program cost? Are there additional fees?

The total cost is $10,000.00 or less for qualified students. There is a $2,000.00 conversion fee for the 21 hours earned through microcredentials and prior learning experience credits. Students are then billed per credit hour at Texas Tech for remaining course work.

You can get started in the first four micro-credential courses for free and pay later when you convert them to credit.  Also, all eligible prior-learning credits will convert to credit for no cost.

Your advisor will connect you with a financial aid advisor to discuss all financing options.

Would Online+ be a good fit for a student that was not yet mature enough to go to college earlier in life but is now ready to commit to education?

Yes, the Online+ program at Texas Tech University would be a great fit for a student who may not have been ready for college earlier in life but is now committed to pursuing their education. The program is designed specifically for non-traditional students, including those looking to balance their studies with work and life commitments. It offers flexibility with eight-week accelerated courses and asynchronous learning, allowing students to study on their own schedule. Additionally, the program recognizes prior work-life experiences, making it easier for students to earn credit and complete their degree. If you're interested in getting started or want more information, you can visit http://GoOnline.ttu.edu (opens in new tab) or contact the TTU Online+ program at 1-844-691-0494 or online@ttu.edu.

A short help document provided by Texas Tech that explains how to enroll, link accounts, use the Industry Career Certificates program, and where to get help.

Learner support team

Coursera’s help team who assist with account linking, verification, access problems, and other issues related to Coursera courses and certificates.

Learning history

A record of courses, progress, and certificates associated with a user account on a learning platform.

Learning program / learner program

A group or collection of courses or certificates an organization (like TTU) provides to its learners through Coursera.

What are the main advantages of the 10-K program?

Step 1: Affordable – Designed to be completed for $10,000 or less.

Unlike Online Plus, the 10-K program is specifically structured for students completing degrees with prior credits and in-person learning.

Peer-reviewed assignments are graded by learners who are also taking the certificate at the same time. **Prior Learning Assessment (PLA)**

- **Definition**: Prior Learning Assessment (PLA) is a process used by educational institutions to evaluate and recognize learning gained outside a traditional academic environment. This can include work experience, military service, independent study, or other non-credit activities.

- **Purpose**: The goal of PLA is to provide students with academic credit for knowledge and skills they have already acquired, potentially reducing the time and cost required to complete a degree.

- **Application at TTU**: At Texas Tech University, PLA can be used to convert eligible prior learning experiences into academic credit, which can be applied toward degree requirements. This is particularly beneficial for non-traditional students or those with significant professional experience.

For more information or to see if your experiences qualify for PLA, you can contact the TTU Online+ program at 1-844-691-0494 or online@ttu.edu.

Online Master of Professional Accounting

Launch your accounting career and meet CPA exam requirements with Texas Tech’s fully online Master of Professional Accounting. This 30-hour program builds core accounting expertise and prepares you for professional practice and licensure success.

The Online Master of Professional Accounting (MPAcc) at Texas Tech University is a 30-credit-hour graduate program launching in fall 2026, designed for students without an undergraduate accounting degree who want to pursue professional accounting careers and satisfy CPA exam requirements. The curriculum maps to core content areas tested on the CPA exam — including Financial Accounting and Reporting (FAR), Auditing and Attestation (AUD), Taxation and Regulation (REG) and Information Systems and Controls (ISC) — while developing technical proficiency and professional competencies needed in public accounting, industry and non-profit environments. Students study taxation, auditing, accounting information systems, advanced accounting topics, ethics and business law. Delivered fully online and asynchronously, the program provides flexibility for working professionals and prepares graduates to excel as accounting practitioners, leaders and strategic contributors in a wide range of organizations.

Prepare for leadership in the sport industry with Texas Tech’s fully online Master of Science in Sport Management. This 30-credit-hour program develops strategic, operational and revenue-focused expertise for careers in collegiate athletics, professional sports and sport-related organizations.

Texas Tech University’s Online Master of Science in Sport Management is a 30-credit-hour graduate program designed to prepare students for leadership and administrative roles across the sport industry. The curriculum combines core management principles with specialized coursework in sport law, marketing, revenue generation, player personnel management and organizational leadership. Delivered fully online in an asynchronous format, the program is structured for working professionals seeking advancement in collegiate athletics, professional sport organizations, community recreation and related industries. Students build analytical, financial and strategic decision-making skills while examining the legal, operational and ethical dimensions of sport enterprises. Emphasis is placed on applied learning and industry relevance, preparing graduates to navigate the competitive and evolving landscape of the global sport industry with confidence and strategic insight.

Online Master's Degree in Interdisciplinary Studies

Design a flexible graduate degree that connects your academic interests, professional goals, and real-world experience through Texas Tech Online's Master of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies or Master of Science in Interdisciplinary Sciences.

Texas Tech University's 30-hour online master's degree in interdisciplinary studies or interdisciplinary sciences allows students to build a customized graduate program by combining approved Online+ academic areas. Students may pursue either the Master of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies or the Master of Science in Interdisciplinary Sciences based on academic interests and selected coursework. The M.A. is designed for students whose interests align more closely with non-STEM fields, while the M.S. requires students to complete at least 18 credit hours of approved STEM coursework as part of the degree plan.

Students can connect multiple disciplines to prepare for career advancement, professional transitions, doctoral study or specialized work that does not fit within a single traditional program. Courses are delivered in 8-week asynchronous Online+ formats designed to support working professionals and adult learners. Students work with advisors to develop a coherent plan of study aligned with academic and professional goals.

As professional environments continue to evolve, employers increasingly value individuals who can integrate knowledge across disciplines, communicate effectively across diverse perspectives and adapt to complex challenges that extend beyond traditional academic boundaries.
